title: A 50-Gram Songbird Kills Mice and Hangs Them on Thorns

scenes.text: This little songbird keeps a butcher's shop.
It weighs about fifty grams, yet it takes mice, lizards, even birds near its own weight.
It bites the neck and shakes its head eleven times a second.
That whips the prey at six g, like a human head in a rear-end car crash.
Its feet are too weak to hold a carcass, so it impales kills on thorns and barbed wire and tears them apart.
scenes.keywords: loggerhead shrike impaled prey barbed wire

scenes.text: The spikes double as a shop window. Males with the fullest larders breed first. A butcher's shop, open for business.

description:
The loggerhead shrike, a 50-gram songbird nicknamed the butcherbird, kills mice, lizards and small birds by biting the neck and shaking its head about 11 times a second, whipping the prey at around 6 g, then impales the bodies on thorns and barbed wire because its feet are too weak to hold them.
The larder stores food and, in related shrikes, males with the biggest caches breed first (Sustaita et al., Biology Letters, 2018).
What is the scariest small bird you have seen?
subject: loggerhead shrike
first_comment: Shrikes even impale toxic grasshoppers and leave them for days until the poison fades. Which bird would you never have guessed was a predator?
